title: Denmark concert with Svend Asmussen, Valaida Snow and Freddie Crump
summary: Just before the Germans took Denmark he played a concert at Karpehollen with Svend Asmussen, Leo Mathisen, Roland Smith, Louis Sims, and mentions Valaida Snow and drummer Freddie Crump.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, there was a man, fellow named Sven Asmussen, come from Denmark. He looked like Stuff Smith, and he played just like Stuff Smith. He was a Dane, the swingingest rascal you ever heard. On the violin.
Oh, you mean after Stuff Smith?
Asmussen, he was a jazz man, beautiful.
And during my stay I made a concert just before the Germans took Denmark at a place called Karpehollen.
There was Sven Asmussen, a trombone player named Leo Matissen, and you had a saxophone player, his name was Roland Smith, and we had a singer, boy, he was from here. Louis Sims.
And by the way, a great woman trumpet player, her name was Valaida Snow (phomatic). She could sing, play the piano, play the violin, act, she was a genius. She was up there, in Denmark.
Seemed like another drummer, his name was Freddie the Popa Jones Crump. Now, he was, -- That old man is something else.
When you hear him, you understand what I mean.
Well, I don't know. Freddie Crump. He might be from -- somewhere in the Carolinas, Georgia, somewhere in the South like that.

Freddie Crump, keep in mind. He married a judge's daughter or some legislative -- some legislator's daughter and he got along playing drums -- got them all playing drums -- men and women now, oh yes, for a long time they was men and women. Pretty as they could be.
And then, after I played that concert it seemed like the Germans took Denmark.
